A few Android settings need to be turned on for MAD Launcher to fully work. Tap a step to jump straight to it.
Set MAD Launcher as your Home app
This is what actually replaces your stock home screen. Without it, pressing Home won\'t bring up any of this.
Real alerts, unread icons, in-window reply, and the persistent media chips all need notification access.
Needed for nav shortcuts, MAD floating windows, and sticky notes that stay on top of other apps.
Turn on accessibility for nav shortcuts
The round bell and gear sit on the system 3-button nav bar in every app. Screen content is not read.
Action Box shows recent app threads first, then your phone contacts for @ # *.
Local reminder toasts from MAD Launcher.
Keeps the notification listener from being silently killed in the background.
Lets Recents and Most used include apps opened from other apps — the same list Android keeps for the Overview screen.
Coarse location only, so the home weather widget can show a real temperature.
Fallback when your phone does not mirror SMS to notification access — unread counts, MAD Messages rows, and alert sound from the SMS inbox.
Type ! then a site (e.g. !yt cats, !w paris). !+YouTube cats searches any app. Save your own !word under ! settings — an app, or a search= link.
Pick a messaging or email app, then a contact — Action box opens that chat ready to type. Aliases: txt, text, msg, message, mail, email, send.
Type : then pick an installed social app (including Facebook). Action box opens the composer. No auto-post.
Type & then a name (or & then Space) — pick the person, then choose an app to message or call them. Also works with the word “contact”.
Type ? then your question; pick an assistant if several are installed. Aliases: ai, ask ai.
No AI assistants found. Install ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, or similar.
Find a contact, then message or call
Pick a calling app (Phone, WhatsApp, Messenger, …), then a recent conversation. Aliases: dial, call, phone.
Pick a video-calling app, then a recent conversation. Aliases: vid, video.
Type /n then Space — pick a notes app (Keep, etc.) and create the note there.
Type /a or add contact then Space — name and optional number, then pick your Contacts app. Opens the add-contact screen.
Type /t, trans, or translate then Space — the field clears for your text. Optional: from english to spanish. Translation runs on this phone, or pick a translator app.
Saves a sticky note on the home screen. Does not open other apps.
Opens Clock. /r or remind, then milk in 20 min for a timer, or pickup at 8pm for an alarm.

MAD windows, Recents, and nav shortcuts
These extras replace system Recents, the notification shade, and Quick Settings. They are off by default because they do not work reliably on many phones.
MAD Notifications and Quick Settings windows
Off: Notifications opens the notification shade. Quick settings opens the extended shade (same as swiping down twice).
On: Messages, System & apps, and Quick Settings open MAD\'s own windows instead of the system shade.
Off: tap the Action Box pill to type. /h still lists commands.
On: tap the Action Box pill for a menu of commands. /h is unchanged.
Off: the MAD clock widget does not show unread app icons.
On: unread app icons appear on the MAD clock widget.
Off: Recents (pinch-out and Recents actions) opens the phone Overview.
On: Recents opens MAD\'s own recent-apps window. Usage access fills the list from other apps.
Off: no overlay buttons on the nav bar, and MAD does not intercept nav taps. Placements stay saved.
On: overlay buttons and nav taps use your placements. Edit them below.
This needs extra permissions. Open each missing grant, then return here. Cancel leaves it off.
Optional name, email, and notes. Confirm sends a .txt and .json to the MAD GitHub reports folder.
MAD adapts to your phone\'s OS. Limited features stay usable but may not mirror the stock shade exactly.
Some alerts may not match the status bar on this ROM. Dismiss in MAD may not clear the system shade.
View details in Not working settings
%1$d features are limited on this device. Tap for details.
Security app autostart keeps notification mirroring and nav shortcuts alive after reboot.
HyperOS often kills background listeners. Set MAD to unrestricted battery use.
Finish the required permissions above — then MAD runs a compatibility self-test here.
Helps MAD learn what works on your phone. Re-check re-runs the probe. Upload sends the report to GitHub reports/compat.
Re-check only re-runs the probe. Upload sends a self-test to GitHub reports/compat. Bug reports use Extras.
System follows the phone’s dark and light setting. Nord, Wallpaper, and Steampunk still switch with it.

Layout stays put — nothing scales or slides. Icons and names turn together in place. MAD clock stays stacked (clock, date, weather) and fills its cell; wide third-party strips stay as drawn. Leave off on tablets.
